downgrade:anti-gravity-gain-redesigned.detail: 4.4 replaced the anti-gravity algorithm and cut the gain range from 0-30000 to 0-250, with the default going from 3500 to 80. No single formula turns one scale into the other, and a 4.4 value used with the 4.3 math would give almost no anti-gravity.
downgrade:anti-gravity-gain-redesigned.note: Anti-gravity strength is measured on a different scale in 4.3.2, and your 4.4.3 value has no equivalent, so it is set back to the 4.3.2 default with `set anti_gravity_gain = 3500`. If you had tuned anti-gravity, retune it on 4.3.2.

downgrade:baro-2smpb-02b-not-in-4-3.detail: PR #11173 added 2SMPB_02B to the barometer list in 4.4. All the other barometer names are the same in both versions.
downgrade:baro-2smpb-02b-not-in-4-3.note: 4.3.2 has no 2SMPB_02B barometer option, so the board's own default barometer setting applies. A 2SMPB_02B sensor can't be selected on 4.3.2.

downgrade:debug-modes-added-in-4-4.detail: 4.4 added several debug modes, for example FAILSAFE in PR #12195 and DSHOT_TELEMETRY_COUNTS in PR #12709. All the 4.3.2 names still exist in 4.4, but the new ones have no counterpart in 4.3.2.
downgrade:debug-modes-added-in-4-4.note: This debug mode was added in 4.4 and doesn't exist in 4.3.2, so the board's default debug mode applies. It only affects what blackbox logs record, not how the quad flies. If you log for tuning, pick one of the 4.3.2 modes, e.g. `set debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED`.

downgrade:displayport-msp-serial-from-po.detail: 4.4 removed this setting. At boot it now picks the first non-USB serial port whose function mask includes MSP DisplayPort. 4.3.2 still reads the port number from this setting.
downgrade:displayport-msp-serial-from-po.note: In 4.3.2 the MSP DisplayPort port is set by this setting, not by a function flag on the port's `serial` line. The converter filled it in from the non-USB port that had MSP and MSP DisplayPort enabled in your serial settings. Check that it points to the port your digital VTX or OSD is wired to.

downgrade:elrs-domain-ce2400-not-in-4-3.detail: 4.4 added CE2400 to the ExpressLRS domain list, a 2.4 GHz domain with reduced telemetry output power. 4.3.2's default is the first entry its build has: AU433 when the board has a 433/868/915 MHz radio, ISM2400 when it has only a 2.4 GHz one.
downgrade:elrs-domain-ce2400-not-in-4-3.note: 4.3.2 has no CE2400 domain, so this line is left out and your board's 4.3.2 default applies: ISM2400 on a flight controller whose receiver is 2.4 GHz only. ISM2400 is the same band, but it doesn't use CE2400's reduced telemetry power. Check that the domain matches your transmitter, e.g. `get expresslrs_domain`.

downgrade:elrs-uid-same-layout.detail: The stored 6-byte UID has the same layout in both versions. Only the over-the-air protocol changed, and that is what stops ELRS 3.x and 2.x from binding to each other.
downgrade:elrs-uid-same-layout.note: Your binding UID carries over unchanged, but the built-in ExpressLRS receiver changes from ELRS 3.x in Betaflight 4.4 to ELRS 2.x in 4.3, and the two can't bind to each other. If your transmitter module runs ELRS 3.x, put ELRS 2.x firmware on it before flying.

downgrade:feedforward-smooth-factor-max-.detail: PR #12426 raised the maximum of feedforward_smooth_factor from 75 to 95 to suit the ELRS 1000 Hz link rate. 4.3.2 still has the old limit.
downgrade:feedforward-smooth-factor-max-.note: 4.3.2 allows feedforward smoothing only up to 75. Values up to 75 carry over unchanged, and higher values were lowered to 75. That means slightly less smoothing on very fast links, such as ELRS at 1000 Hz.

downgrade:gps-rescue-angle-from-max-angl.detail: The same stored field: 4.3.2's gps_rescue_angle (0-200) was renamed in 4.4.0, and again in 4.4.1 to gps_rescue_max_angle, when PR #12413 set its range to 0-80.
downgrade:gps-rescue-angle-from-max-angl.note: Your 4.4.3 GPS Rescue maximum angle carries over with the same number. In 4.4 it limits pitch, reduced when ground speed is off target, and limits roll to half of it. In 4.3.2 it limits pitch only, with no speed scaling. Test GPS Rescue in a safe place before relying on it.

downgrade:gps-rescue-ascend-rate-clamp.detail: 4.4 lowered the minimum of this setting from 100 to 50 cm/s. The units are unchanged.
downgrade:gps-rescue-ascend-rate-clamp.note: 4.3.2's lowest allowed GPS Rescue climb rate is 100 cm/s. Values from 100 up carry over unchanged, and lower values were raised to 100, so the rescue climbs a little faster.

downgrade:gps-rescue-descend-rate-clamp.detail: 4.4 lowered the minimum of this setting from 100 to 25 cm/s. The units are unchanged.
downgrade:gps-rescue-descend-rate-clamp.note: 4.3.2's lowest allowed GPS Rescue descent rate is 100 cm/s. Values from 100 up carry over unchanged, and lower values were raised to 100, so the rescue descends faster than you had it set.

downgrade:gps-rescue-descent-dist-min-30.detail: PR #12835 lowered the minimum to 10 in 4.4. 4.3.2 keeps the older 30-500 range for the same meter-based setting.
downgrade:gps-rescue-descent-dist-min-30.note: The descent distance is still in meters, but 4.3.2 accepts only 30 to 500. Values from 30 up carry over unchanged, and anything below 30 becomes 30.

downgrade:gps-rescue-ground-speed-min-30.detail: In 4.4 the minimum for this setting was lowered to 0 cm/s. 4.3.2 still enforces a minimum of 30.
downgrade:gps-rescue-ground-speed-min-30.note: The return ground speed is still in cm/s, but 4.3.2 accepts only 30 to 3000. Values from 30 up carry over unchanged, and anything below 30 becomes 30.

downgrade:gps-rescue-initial-alt-from-re.detail: In 4.4, gps_rescue_initial_alt was renamed gps_rescue_return_alt and its range was widened to 2-255 m. This setting is the same field under its 4.3.2 name.
downgrade:gps-rescue-initial-alt-from-re.note: Your 4.4.3 return altitude is carried into this 4.3.2 setting, still in meters. 4.3.2 accepts only 20 to 100 m, so a lower value is raised to 20 and a higher one is lowered to 100.

downgrade:gps-rescue-landing-alt-clamp.detail: In 4.4 the range was widened to 1-15 m. 4.3.2 keeps the narrower 3-10 range.
downgrade:gps-rescue-landing-alt-clamp.note: The landing altitude is still in meters, but 4.3.2 accepts only 3 to 10. A lower value is raised to 3 and a higher one is lowered to 10.

downgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-from-min-st.detail: In 4.3.2, a rescue started closer than gps_rescue_min_dth (50-1000 m) is marked too close. PR #12835 changed the setting to a 10-30 m distance that the quad flies out to before turning home.
downgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-from-min-st.note: This value comes from your 4.4.3 gps_rescue_min_start_dist, but the setting works differently in 4.3.2. Here it is the home distance below which a GPS rescue is refused, and a rescue refused during failsafe disarms the quad. Every 4.4.3 value (10-30) becomes 50, the 4.3.2 minimum, so check that this suits where you fly.

downgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-rename-clam.detail: PR #12835 reworked GPS Rescue for 4.4 so that a rescue started too close flies out to this distance before returning. In 4.3.2, the same field marks the rescue as too close, and that disarms the quad when the rescue starts from failsafe.
downgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-rename-clam.note: This distance means something different in 4.3.2. In 4.4.3, a rescue started closer to home than this distance made the quad climb and fly out past it, then return normally. In 4.3.2, a rescue started that close is refused, and in failsafe the quad disarms and drops. Check that this is safe where you fly, for example if a failsafe could happen near home.

downgrade:gps-rescue-return-alt-renamed-.detail: In 4.4, gps_rescue_initial_alt was renamed gps_rescue_return_alt and its range was widened to 2-255 m.
downgrade:gps-rescue-return-alt-renamed-.note: In 4.3.2 this setting is called gps_rescue_initial_alt, so the value moves to that name, still in meters. 4.3.2 accepts only 20 to 100 m, so a lower value is raised to 20 and a higher one is lowered to 100.

downgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-d-rewritte.detail: Between 4.3.2 and 4.4.3 the throttle D path was rewritten several times: the old scaled controller was replaced, the derivative was changed to a pt2-filtered term, and PR #12835 added a descent-rate multiplier. The 4.3.2 range is 0-500, with a default of 50 on boards with GPS Rescue.
downgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-d-rewritte.note: 4.3.2 uses an older GPS Rescue altitude controller where this throttle D gain has a different scale and filtering, so your 4.4.3 value means something else there. The 4.3.2 default is used instead; test GPS Rescue in a safe place before relying on it, and retune if needed.

downgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-i-rewritte.detail: In 4.4.3 the I term is integrated over the altitude data interval with different scaling, replacing the older scaled controller that 4.3.2 uses. The 4.3.2 range is 0-500, with a default of 20 on boards with GPS Rescue.
downgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-i-rewritte.note: 4.3.2 uses an older GPS Rescue altitude controller where this throttle I gain has different scaling and timing, so your 4.4.3 value can't be converted. The 4.3.2 default is used instead; test GPS Rescue in a safe place before relying on it, and retune if needed.

downgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-p-rewritte.detail: 4.4.3 multiplies throttle P by altitude error in metres, replacing the older scaled controller that 4.3.2 uses; the defaults differ about 10x (150 in 4.3.2 vs 15 in 4.4.3 on boards with GPS Rescue). The 4.3.2 range is 0-500.
downgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-p-rewritte.note: 4.3.2 uses an older GPS Rescue altitude controller with a different error basis and scale, so your 4.4.3 throttle P gain can't be converted. The 4.3.2 default is used instead; test GPS Rescue in a safe place before relying on it, and retune if needed.

downgrade:gps-rescue-velocity-controller.detail: Between 4.3.2 and 4.4.3 the GPS Rescue velocity controller was rewritten. The old integer controller added its output to the pitch angle step by step, while the new float PID sets the pitch angle directly. PR #12413 later changed the D-term normalisation and filtering, the I-term relax and the pitch limits. The gains are on different scales, and the allowed range also differs (0-500 in 4.3.2, 0-255 in 4.4.3).
downgrade:gps-rescue-velocity-controller.note: GPS Rescue's velocity-to-pitch controller works differently in 4.3.2, so your 4.4.3 velocity gains don't carry over and 4.3.2's own defaults are used instead. If you tuned these gains, retune them in 4.3.2 and test GPS Rescue in a safe place before you rely on it.

downgrade:gps-rescue-yaw-p-now-real-gain.detail: 4.3.2's GPS Rescue code only sets this gain's default; the setting appears in the OSD menu and MSP, but no flight code reads it.
downgrade:gps-rescue-yaw-p-now-real-gain.note: In 4.4.3 this gain steers the heading during GPS Rescue. 4.3.2 stores and displays it, but its GPS Rescue never reads it, so it has no effect there.

downgrade:osd-display-name-pos-from-pilo.detail: The element was renamed from display_name to pilot_name, with the same position index, type and range. The 4.3.2 position format can't hold the HD column, so the converter clears the position in that case and keeps the rest of the value.
downgrade:osd-display-name-pos-from-pilo.note: The OSD pilot name element has its older name, display name, in 4.3.2, and your position carries over. If the element sat in a column that only exists on HD OSDs, it moves to the top-left corner (0,0), so check where it sits in the OSD layout.

downgrade:osd-esc-temp-alarm-off-sentine.detail: In 4.4.3 the setting became unsigned (0 to 255) and 0 became 'off'. In 4.3.2 it is signed (-128 to 127) and -128 means 'off'.
downgrade:osd-esc-temp-alarm-off-sentine.note: Your ESC temperature alarm carries over. An alarm that was off (0) is written as -128, which means off in 4.3.2. Values above 127 are capped at 127, the highest value 4.3.2 accepts.

downgrade:osd-hd-column-position-reset-1.detail: PR #11964 added bit 10 of each OSD position as a sixth column bit, allowing HD columns 32-63. 4.3.2 ignores that bit, so the converter clears the column and row bits and keeps only the profile visibility bits.
downgrade:osd-hd-column-position-reset-1.note: This OSD element was placed in an HD column (32 or more), and 4.3.2 has no HD canvas to show it on. The element now sits in the top-left corner (column 0, row 0) and stays on in the same OSD profiles, so move it back where you want it in the Betaflight Configurator App.

downgrade:osd-hd-column-position-reset-1.detail: PR #11964 added bit 10 of the OSD position value as an extra column bit for HD canvases, and 4.3.2 can't represent it. The converter clears the column and row bits (the lowest 11 bits) and keeps the higher OSD profile visibility bits.
downgrade:osd-hd-column-position-reset-1.note: These OSD elements were placed in column 32 or further right on the HD OSD canvas, and 4.3.2 has no HD canvas or columns that far right. Each element keeps its OSD profile visibility but moves to the top-left corner (column 0, row 0). Move the elements back where you want them, for example in the Betaflight Configurator App.

downgrade:osd-pilot-name-pos-renamed.detail: In 4.3.2 this element is called osd_display_name_pos. It was renamed to osd_pilot_name_pos later, with the same item index and value format. The converter keeps the visibility bits and clears the position bits, because 4.3.2 can't show a position on the HD canvas.
downgrade:osd-pilot-name-pos-renamed.note: This OSD element sat in an HD canvas column (32 or more), but Betaflight 4.3.2 has only the 30-column canvas. It stays switched on but moves to the top-left corner (column 0, row 0), where other moved elements may stack on it. Move it back where you want it in the Betaflight Configurator App, or set its position with osd_display_name_pos.

downgrade:osd-pos-encoding-same-low-colu.detail: PR #11964 added HD OSD support by using bit 10 of each element position as an extra column bit, which allows columns 32-63. PR #12038 fixed how that bit is read. 4.3.2 ignores the bit, so these positions can't be shown as they were.
downgrade:osd-pos-encoding-same-low-colu.note: This OSD element sat in an HD canvas column (32 or more), but 4.3.2 only has the 30-column canvas. The element stays switched on but goes to the top-left corner (column 0, row 0), and any other moved elements will stack on top of it there. Before flying, move each one where you want it, for example in the Betaflight Configurator App.

downgrade:osd-pos-encoding-same-low-colu.detail: PR #11964 added HD OSD support and used bit 10 of the position value as an extra column bit for columns 32 and up. 4.3.2 has no such column, so those positions can't carry over. Positions in columns 0-31 are stored the same way in both versions.
downgrade:osd-pos-encoding-same-low-colu.note: This OSD element sat in an HD canvas column (32 or more) that 4.3.2 doesn't have, because 4.3.2 only has the 30-column canvas. The element stays switched on but now appears in the top-left corner (column 0, row 0), and any other elements moved the same way stack on top of it there. Before flying, move each one back to where you want it.

downgrade:osd-rsnr-element-removed.detail: PR #11062 added the RSNR OSD element together with osd_rsnr_pos and osd_rsnr_alarm, and a new RSNR LOW warning.
downgrade:osd-rsnr-element-removed.note: 4.3.2 has no dedicated RSNR OSD element or RSNR alarm, so the RSNR readout and its low-signal warning are not available there. Any RSNR position or alarm you set up will have to be left out.

downgrade:osd-stat-battery-from-bitmask.detail: In 4.4.3 the individual osd_stat_* switches were combined into one osd_stat_bitmask setting. This statistic is bit 7, and the converter reads that bit.
downgrade:osd-stat-battery-from-bitmask.note: In 4.3.2 this post-flight OSD statistic is its own ON/OFF setting. It is set ON or OFF to match your 4.4.3 statistics selection, so nothing needs doing.

downgrade:osd-stat-bb-no-from-bitmask.detail: In 4.4.3 the individual osd_stat_* switches were combined into one osd_stat_bitmask setting. This statistic is bit 13, and the converter reads that bit.
downgrade:osd-stat-bb-no-from-bitmask.note: In 4.3.2 this post-flight OSD statistic is its own ON/OFF setting. It is set ON or OFF to match your 4.4.3 statistics selection, so nothing needs doing.

downgrade:osd-stat-bbox-from-bitmask.note: In 4.3.2 this post-flight OSD statistic is its own ON/OFF setting. It is set ON or OFF to match your 4.4.3 statistics selection, so nothing needs doing.

downgrade:osd-stat-bitmask-split-to-sett.detail: In 4.4.3 the per-statistic osd_stat_* settings were combined into one osd_stat_bitmask on the same stored field, with one bit per statistic. On downgrade, each old setting reads its own bit back. Bits for statistics added after 4.3.2 have no setting to go to.
downgrade:osd-stat-bitmask-split-to-sett.note: In 4.3.2 each post-flight OSD statistic has its own ON/OFF setting, such as osd_stat_battery or osd_stat_max_alt. They are set to match your bitmask. Statistics that 4.3.2 doesn't have can't carry over.

downgrade:osd-stat-endbatt-from-bitmask.note: 4.3.2 has a separate ON/OFF setting for the end-of-flight battery statistic. Its value was read from your osd_stat_bitmask, so whether the stat is shown stays the same. Nothing to do.

downgrade:serial-vtx-msp-bit-downgrade.detail: 4.4 added the VTX_MSP serial function (bit value 131072). 4.3.2 doesn't have it and resets every port's settings if a serial line contains it, so the converter clears that bit.
downgrade:serial-vtx-msp-bit-downgrade.note: In 4.4 this port had VTX (MSP) on without MSP, which means VTX control over the receiver link (e.g. CRSF). Betaflight 4.3 can't control the VTX over the receiver link, so that function was taken off this port. Set up VTX control another way, such as SmartAudio or Tramp on a UART.

downgrade:stats-mah-used-removed.detail: PR #11084 added battery continuation using persistent stats, and PR #11671 reworked the OSD stats and warnings settings. The same changes also removed battery_continue in 4.3.2.
downgrade:stats-mah-used-removed.note: This value was a stored stat tied to the battery continuation feature, which 4.3.2 doesn't have. There is nothing to set again, and the stored value isn't carried over.

downgrade:vcd-video-system-hd-not-in-4-3.detail: PR #11964 added the HD video system and HD OSD support in 4.4, so 4.3.2 has no equivalent. PR #12152 makes the firmware fall back to AUTO when HD isn't supported.
downgrade:vcd-video-system-hd-not-in-4-3.note: 4.3.2 only offers AUTO, PAL and NTSC for the video system, so your HD choice can't be kept and the setting now uses the 4.3.2 default, AUTO. Check that your OSD looks right before flying. If you need a fixed analog standard, use `set vcd_video_system = PAL` or `set vcd_video_system = NTSC`.

upgrade:anti-gravity-mode-removed.detail: The 4.4 anti-gravity rewrite (commit 6aaaf727ff86, no PR number) removed the mode selector and its lookup table and rewrote the algorithm without a mode switch.
upgrade:anti-gravity-mode-removed.note: 4.4.3 has no SMOOTH/STEP choice, so there is nothing to set for it. Anti-gravity now works differently and is tuned with `anti_gravity_cutoff_hz` and `anti_gravity_p_gain`, which are not equivalents of the old mode. They start at their defaults, so check how the quad behaves on throttle punches.

upgrade:anti-gravity-redesigned-gain-res.detail: For 4.4, anti-gravity was rewritten: the old high-pass-filtered I-term and P-term boost was replaced by a boost driven by how fast the throttle moves, with no boost on yaw. The maximum dropped from 30000 to 250 and the default changed from 3500 to 80, so no single formula reproduces the old behaviour.
upgrade:anti-gravity-redesigned-gain-res.note: Anti-gravity uses a new algorithm and a new 0-250 scale in 4.4.3, so your old value can't be converted. The 4.4.3 default of 80 is used instead. If you had tuned anti-gravity, retune it on the new scale, e.g. `set anti_gravity_gain = 80`, then adjust from there.

upgrade:crsf-use-rx-snr-removed.detail: PR #11062 added RSNR to the OSD and removed the crsf_use_rx_snr setting and its field.
upgrade:crsf-use-rx-snr-removed.note: If you used the option to show SNR in place of RSSI, 4.4.3 has a separate RSNR OSD element for it. RSSI now always shows RSSI dBm. To show SNR, enable the RSNR element and set its position with `osd_rsnr_pos`; `osd_rsnr_alarm` sets its alarm.

upgrade:elrs-uid-meaning-unchanged.detail: The stored 6-byte UID has the same layout in both versions. Only the over-the-air protocol changed, and that is what stops ELRS 2.x and 3.x from binding to each other.
upgrade:elrs-uid-meaning-unchanged.note: Your binding UID carries over unchanged, but the built-in ExpressLRS receiver changes from ELRS 2.x in Betaflight 4.3 to ELRS 3.x in 4.4, and the two can't bind to each other. If your transmitter module runs ELRS 2.x, update it to ELRS 3.x before flying.

upgrade:esc-temp-alarm-off-value-moved-t.detail: The Extended Bidir DShot commit changed the ESC temperature alarm from a signed (-128 to 127) to an unsigned (0 to 255) value and moved the off value from -128 to 0.
upgrade:esc-temp-alarm-off-value-moved-t.note: The value that turns this alarm off is now 0 instead of -128. An alarm that was off stays off. A negative temperature also becomes 0, which now means off. Positive temperatures carry over unchanged.

upgrade:gps-rescue-angle-renamed-max-ang.detail: PR #12413 renamed the old rescue angle to gps_rescue_max_angle with a range of 0-80 and used it as the pitch angle limit. PR #12854 kept that 0-80 range.
upgrade:gps-rescue-angle-renamed-max-ang.note: Your GPS Rescue angle carries over under its new name. It now has a range of 0-80 degrees, so any value above 80 is capped at 80. If you had a higher value, the rescue will now fly at a lower maximum angle.

upgrade:gps-rescue-initial-alt-renamed-r.detail: A Betaflight commit renamed gps_rescue_initial_alt to gps_rescue_return_alt on the same field. The new 2-255 range covers the old 20-100.
upgrade:gps-rescue-initial-alt-renamed-r.note: Your GPS Rescue return altitude carries over unchanged under its new name. It's the same setting in metres, and every old value is valid in the new range. Nothing to do.

upgrade:gps-rescue-landing-dist-removed.detail: The GPS Rescue refactoring and landing improvements (commit a6507c02d96f, no PR number) removed the setting and the landing-box logic.
upgrade:gps-rescue-landing-dist-removed.note: Nothing replaces the landing distance, so there is no value to set again. GPS Rescue in 4.4.3 decides when to land by altitude only, so check your rescue landing behaviour before relying on it.

upgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-renamed-min-s.detail: PR #12835 changed what happens when a rescue starts inside this distance: the quad now flies outward before turning home, instead of refusing the rescue or disarming. This setting replaces 4.3's gps_rescue_min_dth.
upgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-renamed-min-s.note: GPS Rescue now behaves differently close to home. In 4.3, a rescue started closer to home than this distance was refused, and in failsafe the quad disarmed and dropped. In 4.4 the quad climbs and flies out past this distance, then does a normal rescue, so check that this suits where you fly.

upgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-renamed-min-s.detail: PR #12835 set the 10-30 range and added the fly-outward behaviour for rescues started too close to home. An earlier commit had moved the old minimum-distance field to the name gps_rescue_min_start_dist.
upgrade:gps-rescue-min-dth-renamed-min-s.note: The old minimum distance (50-1000 m) doesn't fit the new 10-30 m range, so your value always becomes 30. The setting also works differently now: if a rescue starts closer to home than this, the quad flies outward first and then turns for home. It no longer refuses the rescue or disarms.

upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-d-rewritten.detail: The old controller's D term was replaced by a new altitude-error PID, then changed again to use pt2-filtered altitude data, and PR #12835 added a descent-rate multiplier before the filter. The range also shrank from 0-500 to 0-255.
upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-d-rewritten.note: The GPS Rescue altitude controller was rewritten for 4.4.3, so old throttle D gains don't mean the same thing any more. Your board's 4.4.3 default applies. Test GPS Rescue somewhere safe before relying on it, and retune only if the default doesn't hold altitude well.

upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-i-rescaled.detail: The old controller was replaced by a new altitude-error PID, and the I term now integrates over the actual altitude-data interval with a different scale factor. The range shrank from 0-500 to 0-255.
upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-i-rescaled.note: The GPS Rescue altitude controller was rewritten for 4.4.3, so old throttle I gains don't mean the same thing any more. Your board's 4.4.3 default applies. Test GPS Rescue somewhere safe before relying on it, and retune only if the default doesn't hold altitude well.

upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-p-rescaled.detail: The old controller was replaced by a new PID that works on altitude error in metres, and the default dropped roughly tenfold. The range shrank from 0-500 to 0-255.
upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-p-rescaled.note: The GPS Rescue altitude controller was rewritten for 4.4.3, so old throttle P gains don't mean the same thing any more. Your board's 4.4.3 default applies. Test GPS Rescue somewhere safe before relying on it, and retune only if the default doesn't hold altitude well.

upgrade:gps-rescue-velocity-controller-r.detail: In 4.3.2 the gains drove an integer controller that nudged the pitch angle a little each cycle. In 4.4.3 they feed a float PID that sets the pitch angle directly, with new I limits and D filtering (PR #12413). The allowed range also narrowed from 0-500 to 0-255.
upgrade:gps-rescue-velocity-controller-r.note: GPS Rescue's speed (pitch) controller was rebuilt in 4.4.3 on a different scale, so your old velocity P, I and D gains have no equivalent and the 4.4.3 defaults apply. If you had tuned them, start from the defaults, retune if needed, and test GPS Rescue in a safe place before relying on it.

upgrade:gps-rescue-yaw-p-now-active.detail: In 4.4.3 the GPS Rescue rewrite turns the heading by the heading error times this gain. The range narrowed from 0-500 to 0-255.
upgrade:gps-rescue-yaw-p-now-active.note: 4.3.2 only stored and displayed this gain; its GPS Rescue never read it in flight. In 4.4.3 it sets how hard the quad turns its heading toward home. Test GPS Rescue before relying on it.

upgrade:osd-stats-folded-into-bitmask.detail: A Betaflight commit replaced every osd_stat_* on/off setting with osd_stat_bitmask, a single 32-bit value that uses the same enabled-stats field.
upgrade:osd-stats-folded-into-bitmask.note: The separate on/off settings for each OSD stat are now one number. Each stat you had on sets its own bit, so the same post-flight stats are shown. Nothing to do.

upgrade:osd-warnings-folded-into-bitmask.detail: In 4.4.3 the separate per-warning on/off settings were replaced by a single number, osd_warn_bitmask, where each warning is one bit of the same stored field. The converter adds up the bits for the warnings you had enabled, so each bit keeps its old meaning.
upgrade:osd-warnings-folded-into-bitmask.note: Your OSD warning choices carry over unchanged: each warning you had on stays on and each one you had off stays off. Nothing needs doing. Warnings that are new in 4.4.3 start switched off.

upgrade:rssi-dbm-alarm-range-narrowed.detail: PR #11062 gave SNR its own alarm setting and lowered this alarm's upper limit from 20 to 0, the CRSF RSSI maximum.
upgrade:rssi-dbm-alarm-range-narrowed.note: The RSSI dBm alarm now goes up to 0 instead of 20, so a positive value is lowered to 0. Real RSSI readings are never above 0 dBm, so values up to 0 carry over unchanged.
